title: Ruz Bukhari (Bukhari Rice)
tagline: Warmly spiced Hejazi rice with chicken, sweet carrots and raisins.
intro: Ruz Bukhari travelled to Makkah with Central Asian pilgrims and settlers from Bukhara, and became a treasured part of Hejazi cuisine. Basmati is cooked with chicken, a warm spice blend, sweet grated carrots and raisins, giving a gently sweet-savoury pilaf with a signature amber colour. It is a staple of Makkah's homes and restaurants alike.

items: 1 tbsp Bukhari spice mix (cumin, coriander, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, black lime, black pepper)
500 g (2½ cups) basmati rice, soaked 30 min
2 large carrots, coarsely grated or julienned

method: Brown the onions in oil, add the garlic and chicken and sear.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, Bukhari spices and salt; cook until the oil separates.
Add the water, cover and simmer until the chicken is tender, about 30 minutes. Reserve the chicken; strain and measure about 1 litre of broth.
In the same pot, briefly sauté the grated carrots until softened, then add the raisins.
Add the drained rice and the measured broth; check salt.
Boil, then cover and cook on low until absorbed, 15–18 minutes. Rest 5 minutes.
Broil the chicken for colour if you like, then serve it over the fluffed rice.
tips: The carrots and raisins give Bukhari rice its gentle sweetness — don't leave them out.
Cook the carrots in the spiced broth's oil so they carry the flavour into the rice.
toServe: Serve with daqoos and a fresh salad.
